Class RcxBrick

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.api.lego.RcxBrick
public final class RcxBrick extends Object
Direct commands to an RCX brick that answer back, over the same infrared link as RcxRemote (set it up with RcxRemote.begin(int, int) first, with both the IR LED and the IR receiver module wired). It reads the touch sensors plugged into the RCX's own inputs, so a vehicle can sense obstacles without extra wiring to the Arduino. Plain Java on Infrared.

Each call is a request and a reply, which takes 100 ms or more; they return -1 when the brick does not answer (out of range, off, or the IR LED not pointing at it). The opcode and argument encodings come from the published RCX opcode tables and have not been verified on a brick.

    • drive

      public static void drive(int outputs, int speed)
      Runs the outputs at speed, -7..7: the sign is the direction, the size the power level, and 0 brakes them. That is up to four commands, each waiting for the brick's acknowledgement when the receiver is wired, so one call takes a few hundred milliseconds; set the speed once and not in a tight loop.

    • batteryMillivolts

      public static int batteryMillivolts()
      The brick's battery voltage in millivolts (about 9000 with fresh batteries, and the brick warns below about 6000), or -1 if it did not answer. It is a request and a reply, like the sensor reads.

    • playSound

      public static boolean playSound(int sound)
      Plays one of the six built-in sounds, SOUND_*. Returns whether the brick acknowledged the command, which needs the IR receiver wired; the sound then plays on the brick's own speaker and the call returns without waiting for it to end.

    • playTone

      public static boolean playTone(int frequencyHz, int durationCentiseconds)
      Plays a tone of frequencyHz (about 31 to 20000 Hz) for durationCentiseconds hundredths of a second (1..255, so up to 2.55 s), then returns without waiting for it to end. Returns whether the brick acknowledged the command. A tone replaces any sound still playing, so wait for the duration before sending the next.

    • isPressed

      public static boolean isPressed(int input)
      Whether the touch sensor on input is pressed; false also when the brick did not answer.
